rootMeaning: The word כְּהֻנָּה (kᵉhunnâh) derives from the root כָּהַן (kâhan), which means to serve or minister as a priest. This root conveys the active role of officiating in priestly duties, emphasizing the execution of the priest's office rather than a mere title. Thus, the root meaning enriches the common English gloss 'priesthood' by highlighting the functional and ministerial aspect of the office as one of active service and sacred responsibility.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, כְּהֻנָּה is consistently used to denote the priesthood or the office held by priests, appearing 14 times with translations such as 'priesthood,' 'your priest's office,' and 'of the priesthood.' This consistency underscores its primary focus on the institution and function of priestly service, including its perpetuity and the covenantal role of the Levites and Aaronic priesthood. The range of translations reflects both the collective office and individual responsibilities inherent in the priesthood.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כְּהֻנָּה as the priestly office rooted in active ministry deepens our appreciation of the sacred calling God placed on His servants. It reminds believers that priesthood is not merely a status but a divinely appointed role of mediation, worship, and consecration. This concept points forward to Christ, the ultimate High Priest who perfectly fulfills the priestly function by interceding for His people and offering Himself as the perfect sacrifice. Recognizing the priesthood's perpetual statute also highlights God's faithfulness in establishing a means for His people to approach Him, a foundation that finds its fulfillment in the New Covenant.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 29:9 states, 'And thou shalt gird them with girdles, Aaron and his sons, and put the bonnets on them: and the priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute.' Here, כְּהֻנָּה underscores the conferral of a lasting, divinely ordained priestly role upon Aaron and his sons. The word conveys not only the formal investiture but also the enduring nature of their sacred service, emphasizing God's intention for a continual priestly ministry established by His command.
